items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You see him with Piron’s band. You see him with Papa Celestin’s band, because them two brothers was rated.

ctx.x: How did he sound? There’s not much . . . George Boyd never recorded.

No. They all had that sound of bending notes, playing the blues and all, but they all played in tune. They never deviated from playing some other notes or bending a note wrong. They played within the context of the music. That’s what’s got to be watched when you’re playing a clarinet. You got to play that [expletive deleted] in tune, because it reflects. You got a problem on a note, [? (inaudible)] if you know it, but you got to play that clarinet in tune. If you play like George Lewis, he was never considered a…
